question_plain: Is any critical input bought from only one supplier?
question_technical: Do you have single-source dependencies for critical inputs?
pain: A critical input depends on one supplier
why: Cyber incidents travel through suppliers. A single source turns their outage into yours.
statement: A critical input depends on one supplier. Cyber incidents travel through suppliers. A single source turns their outage into yours.

question_plain: How much do daily operations depend on digital systems like ordering, scheduling or payments?
question_technical: What is the operational dependency on IT systems (ERP, MES, TMS, payments)?
pain: Most work stops when systems stop
why: The more work runs on systems, the faster an IT outage becomes a stopped operation.
statement: Most work stops when systems stop. The more work runs on systems, the faster an IT outage becomes a stopped operation.

question_plain: Are important data backed up, and have you restored from a backup in the last 12 months?
question_technical: Are critical data backed up with a successful restore test in the last 12 months?

options.plain: Yes, and we tested a restore

pain: Backups have not been proven to restore
why: A backup that was never restored is a guess. Most ransomware recoveries fail at this step.
statement: Backups have not been proven to restore. A backup that was never restored is a guess. Most ransomware recoveries fail at this step.

question_plain: Can suppliers, carriers or IT vendors log in to your systems or equipment from outside?
question_technical: Is third-party remote access enabled to your systems or OT assets?
pain: Outside companies have always-on access
why: Always-on vendor access is one of the most common entry points in supply-chain incidents.
statement: Outside companies have always-on access. Always-on vendor access is one of the most common entry points in supply-chain incidents.

question_plain: Do people need a second step (a code or app) to sign in to email and business systems?
question_technical: Is MFA enforced for email and business-critical applications?
pain: Sign-in relies on a password alone
why: A stolen password alone opens email, and email is how fake invoices and payment changes arrive.
statement: Sign-in relies on a password alone. A stolen password alone opens email, and email is how fake invoices and payment changes arrive.

question_plain: Is there an agreed plan for who decides what when a cyber incident disrupts operations?
question_technical: Is there a documented incident-response playbook that includes operations and supply-chain stakeholders?

options.plain: Yes, and we have practiced it
Informal, people would figure it out

pain: No agreed plan for a cyber disruption
why: Without agreed roles, the first hours go to arguing about who decides, while trucks and lines wait.
statement: No agreed plan for a cyber disruption. Without agreed roles, the first hours go to arguing about who decides, while trucks and lines wait.

question_plain: Do you ask critical suppliers how they would keep working through a cyber incident?
question_technical: Are critical suppliers assessed for cyber continuity in onboarding or reviews?
pain: Suppliers' cyber continuity is unknown
why: You inherit your suppliers' recovery time. Asking is the cheapest way to find out what it is.
statement: Suppliers' cyber continuity is unknown. You inherit your suppliers' recovery time. Asking is the cheapest way to find out what it is.

question_plain: When a supplier asks to change its bank account, do you confirm by calling a number you already had?
question_technical: Are supplier bank-detail change requests verified out-of-band against known contact data?

options.plain: No, an email or letter is enough

pain: Bank-detail changes are accepted without a call-back
why: Fake bank-detail changes from look-alike supplier emails are among the most frequent supply-chain frauds.
statement: Bank-detail changes are accepted without a call-back. Fake bank-detail changes from look-alike supplier emails are among the most frequent supply-chain frauds.

options.plain: We work on paper for a while

pain: The main process has no working fallback
why: This is the process you named as hardest to lose. Its fallback decides how an incident feels on the floor.
statement: The main process has no working fallback. This is the process you named as hardest to lose. Its fallback decides how an incident feels on the floor.

question_plain: How long can your most critical process be down before the damage is serious?
question_technical: What is the maximum tolerable downtime of the most critical process?
pain: Very little time before damage is serious
why: This sets the clock. Every recovery answer is compared against it.
statement: Very little time before damage is serious. This sets the clock. Every recovery answer is compared against it.

question_plain: Realistically, how long would it take to get that process working again?
question_technical: What is the practical recovery time (RTO) for that process?
pain: Recovery takes longer than a week
why: Compared with tolerable downtime, this shows whether recovery is fast enough.
statement: Recovery takes longer than a week. Compared with tolerable downtime, this shows whether recovery is fast enough.

question_plain: Are backups kept somewhere an attacker inside your network could not delete them?
question_technical: Are critical backups offline, isolated or immutable?
pain: Backups sit on the same network
why: Attackers delete reachable backups first, then encrypt.
statement: Backups sit on the same network. Attackers delete reachable backups first, then encrypt.

question_plain: Do you know which outside companies can access your systems?
question_technical: Is there a maintained inventory of third parties with system access?
pain: No list of who can get in from outside
why: You cannot close a door you do not know is open.
statement: No list of who can get in from outside. You cannot close a door you do not know is open.

question_plain: Do large or unusual payments need a second person to approve them?
question_technical: Is dual approval enforced for high-value or anomalous payments?
pain: One person can release a large payment
why: A second approver stops most fraudulent transfers, even when the request looks genuine.
statement: One person can release a large payment. A second approver stops most fraudulent transfers, even when the request looks genuine.

question_plain: Is there a named person who can decide to stop or slow operations during a cyber incident?
question_technical: Is authority to degrade or halt operations during an incident assigned?
pain: Nobody is named to stop operations
why: Stopping early can limit spread, but only someone with authority will do it.
statement: Nobody is named to stop operations. Stopping early can limit spread, but only someone with authority will do it.

question_plain: If someone got into your office computers, could they reach the machines that run production?
question_technical: Can corporate IT networks directly reach OT/production systems?
pain: Office and plant systems share one network
why: Office-to-plant paths are how ransomware reaches lines that never touch email.
statement: Office and plant systems share one network. Office-to-plant paths are how ransomware reaches lines that never touch email.

question_plain: Could a wrong or malicious command make equipment behave unsafely?
question_technical: Could malicious digital commands cause unsafe equipment behaviour or hazardous conditions?
pain: Digital commands can create unsafe conditions
why: Where cyber meets physical safety, consequence outranks any technical score.
statement: Digital commands can create unsafe conditions. Where cyber meets physical safety, consequence outranks any technical score.

question_plain: If you lose control or visibility of equipment, can it go to a safe state on its own?
question_technical: Is there a tested safe degraded or shutdown state on loss of control/visibility?
pain: No tested safe state for equipment
why: A safe stop limits damage while systems are rebuilt.
statement: No tested safe state for equipment. A safe stop limits damage while systems are rebuilt.

question_plain: Can the line or process keep running by hand, and for how long?
question_technical: What is the manual / degraded-mode capacity and duration?
pain: No manual way to keep running
why: Manual mode buys time for recovery.
statement: No manual way to keep running. Manual mode buys time for recovery.

question_plain: Does the same supplier or service support several of your critical processes?
question_technical: Is there vendor concentration across multiple critical processes or sites?
pain: One provider sits behind several critical processes
why: One provider behind many processes turns a single incident into a company-wide stop.
statement: One provider sits behind several critical processes. One provider behind many processes turns a single incident into a company-wide stop.

question_plain: Could you move the work to another site, line, carrier or supplier?
question_technical: Can production or service be transferred to alternate capacity?
pain: No alternate site, carrier or supplier
why: Alternate capacity is the difference between a slowdown and a stop.
statement: No alternate site, carrier or supplier. Alternate capacity is the difference between a slowdown and a stop.

question_plain: Can you cut off a vendor's access yourself, right away?
question_technical: Can vendor access be revoked promptly and independently?
pain: You cannot cut off vendor access yourself
why: During an incident you may need to close the door before the vendor answers the phone.
statement: You cannot cut off vendor access yourself. During an incident you may need to close the door before the vendor answers the phone.

question_plain: Are admin accounts separate from everyday accounts?
question_technical: Are privileged accounts separated from standard user accounts?
pain: Admin rights used for everyday work
why: Everyday accounts get phished; admin rights on them turn a phish into a takeover.
statement: Admin rights used for everyday work. Everyday accounts get phished; admin rights on them turn a phish into a takeover.

question_plain: How often are critical backups taken?
question_technical: What is the backup frequency relative to the required RPO?
pain: Backups are taken too rarely
why: The gap between backups is the work you would redo by hand.
statement: Backups are taken too rarely. The gap between backups is the work you would redo by hand.

question_plain: When did you last test switching to a backup system or site?
question_technical: When was failover / recovery last exercised?
pain: Failover has never been tested
why: Untested failover tends to fail the first time it is needed.
statement: Failover has never been tested. Untested failover tends to fail the first time it is needed.

question_plain: Do outside carriers sign in to your order or tracking systems, and how?
question_technical: How do carrier partners authenticate to your TMS/order systems?

options.plain: A few, with a second step

pain: Carriers sign in with one password
why: Carrier logins are a path into order data and shipment changes.
statement: Carriers sign in with one password. Carrier logins are a path into order data and shipment changes.

question_plain: How much time do you have before a delay reaches your customer?
question_technical: What buffer exists before downstream impact (time-to-propagation)?
pain: Delays reach customers within minutes
why: Buffer time decides how fast a local outage becomes a customer problem.
statement: Delays reach customers within minutes. Buffer time decides how fast a local outage becomes a customer problem.

question_plain: Do shipments need customs papers, permits or regulated documents to move?
question_technical: Is product movement dependent on regulated electronic documents?
pain: Shipments depend on digital-only documents
why: If the document system stops, the truck stops at the border even when the goods are ready.
statement: Shipments depend on digital-only documents. If the document system stops, the truck stops at the border even when the goods are ready.

question_plain: Who can change supplier bank details in your system?
question_technical: Who has write access to vendor master data in the ERP, and is it logged?

options.plain: A few named people, and changes are logged

pain: Many people can edit supplier bank details
why: Whoever can edit supplier records can redirect payments.
statement: Many people can edit supplier bank details. Whoever can edit supplier records can redirect payments.

question_plain: Would anyone notice the first payment to a new or changed bank account?
question_technical: Are first-time payments to new or modified beneficiary accounts flagged for review?
pain: First payments to new accounts go unnoticed
why: Fraudulent payments usually go to a brand-new account. Flagging it catches what approvals miss.
statement: First payments to new accounts go unnoticed. Fraudulent payments usually go to a brand-new account. Flagging it catches what approvals miss.

question_plain: Do you share sensitive data such as designs, customer lists or prices with suppliers or partners?
question_technical: Is sensitive data (IP, PII, pricing) shared with third parties, and under what controls?
pain: Sensitive data is shared widely with partners
why: Data held by a partner can leak in their incident, not yours.
statement: Sensitive data is shared widely with partners. Data held by a partner can leak in their incident, not yours.

question_plain: Would you find out if that data leaked from a partner?
question_technical: Would third-party exposure of your data be detected or notified?
pain: A partner leak would go unnoticed
why: Most partner leaks are discovered months later, by someone else.
statement: A partner leak would go unnoticed. Most partner leaks are discovered months later, by someone else.

question_plain: Do people share logins for business systems?
question_technical: How prevalent are shared or generic accounts?
pain: Shared logins are common
why: Shared logins cannot be traced or revoked for one person.
statement: Shared logins are common. Shared logins cannot be traced or revoked for one person.

question_plain: How would you first notice that something is wrong in your systems?
question_technical: What is the primary detection channel for abnormal behaviour?

options.plain: A vendor or customer tells us

pain: Problems would be found late or by outsiders
why: Late detection is the most common reason small incidents become long outages.
statement: Problems would be found late or by outsiders. Late detection is the most common reason small incidents become long outages.

question_plain: If email and chat are down, how would you coordinate?
question_technical: Is an alternate communication channel defined and tested?
pain: No way to coordinate without email
why: Incidents often take email down first, exactly when people need to coordinate.
statement: No way to coordinate without email. Incidents often take email down first, exactly when people need to coordinate.

question_plain: When did you last practice a cyber disruption with the operations team?
question_technical: When was a cyber tabletop exercise last performed?
pain: The team has never practiced a cyber disruption
why: A one-hour practice exposes most gaps in a plan.
statement: The team has never practiced a cyber disruption. A one-hour practice exposes most gaps in a plan.

question_plain: Is it written down which processes and sites depend on each other?
question_technical: Are upstream and downstream dependencies documented?
pain: Dependencies between sites are not mapped
why: In large networks, nobody knows the full chain unless it is written down.
statement: Dependencies between sites are not mapped. In large networks, nobody knows the full chain unless it is written down.

question_plain: After one full shift without the critical process, what has happened?
question_technical: What is the impact at the one-shift mark of the impact curve?
pain: One lost shift means penalties or lost customers
why: This shows how quickly an outage turns into money and customers lost.
statement: One lost shift means penalties or lost customers. This shows how quickly an outage turns into money and customers lost.

question_plain: Which protections limit an attacker on critical systems?
question_technical: Which compensating controls materially limit exploitation (segmentation, EDR, allowlisting)?

options.plain: Not sure what is in place

pain: Few protections beyond antivirus
why: Compensating controls change how much a known vulnerability actually matters.
statement: Few protections beyond antivirus. Compensating controls change how much a known vulnerability actually matters.
